title: Chip Tracker — 4-Channel Chiptune Sequencer
description: An NES-style 4-channel step sequencer with real Fourier-synthesized pulse waves, presets, and one-click WAV export.
concept: A pocket-sized chiptune tracker modeled on classic 8-bit sound chips: two duty-cycle pulse channels, a triangle bass channel, and a percussive noise channel, all sequenced on a tappable step grid. Users dial in each pulse channel's duty cycle for authentic thin/fat 8-bit timbres, mute/solo channels, tune tempo and swing, and generate a random riff or load one of three original presets. Finished patterns save to localStorage, export as a real downloadable WAV file, or share as a URL you can send to a friend.
features: 4-channel step sequencer (2 pulse, 1 triangle, 1 noise) with per-channel mute/solo and volume
Continuously tunable duty-cycle pulse waves built from custom Fourier-series PeriodicWave synthesis
Tempo, swing, pattern length (16/32 steps), random riff generator, and 3 original presets
WAV export via OfflineAudioContext (1x/2x/4x loop render) — real downloadable audio file
Named pattern save/load list plus autosave, both in localStorage, and a shareable URL-hash link

interaction.mouse: Click a step to cycle it through the pentatonic scale (or noise types); click again to keep cycling, wrap to clear
interaction.click: Play/Stop transport button starts the lookahead scheduler; Random Riff and preset dropdown instantly repopulate all 4 channels
interaction.touch: All step cells and sliders are touch-friendly with a horizontally scrolling step grid for 32-step patterns on small screens
interaction.keyboard: Standard tab/enter navigation through buttons, sliders, and the save-name text field
